en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
The Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga,
Chapter on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on Umbrellas and Footwear 84.
The Training Rule on Umbrellas and Footwear.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were carrying sunshades and using sandals.
People criticized, complained, and grumbled:
"How can these bhikkhunīs carry sunshades and use sandals? They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so forth]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six use sunshades and sandals?"... [and so forth]...
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs carry sunshades and use sandals?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can the group of six bhikkhunīs carry a sunshade and sandals?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī should carry a sunshade and sandals, there is an offense of wrong-doing."**
“Whichever bhikkhunī should carry a sunshade and sandals, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Thus was this training rule for bhikkhunīs laid down by the Blessed One.
Now at that time, a certain bhikkhunī was ill.
For her, it was not comfortable without a sunshade and sandals...
[they] reported this matter to the Blessed One...
"I allow, monks, a sunshade and sandals for a sick bhikkhunī."
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule thus:
"Whichever nun, not being ill, should carry a sunshade and sandals, it is an offense entailing expiation. Whichever nun...
[the rest follows].
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... [as previously described] ... "a nun" ...
[as previously described] ... this is the nun intended in this context.
"Not ill" means she who feels comfortable without a sunshade and sandals.
"Ill" means...
For one who is not comfortable without a sunshade and sandals.
A "sunshade" refers to three types of sunshades: a white sunshade, a palm-leaf sunshade, and a leaf sunshade; it may be circularly bound or bound with strips.
"Should wear":
if she wears it even once, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one who is not ill, perceiving herself as not ill, wears a sunshade and sandals, there is an offense of expiation.
If one who is not ill, being in doubt, uses a sunshade and sandals, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one who is not ill, perceiving herself to be ill, uses a sunshade and sandals, there is an offense of expiation.
If she uses a sunshade but not sandals, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she wears sandals and carries an umbrella, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she is ill but perceives herself as not ill, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is ill but is uncertain [of her state], there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is ill, but perceives herself as ill, there is no offense.
There is no offense for one who is ill.
If she wears it in a monastery or in the vicinity of a monastery;
in cases of emergency;
or if she is insane.
"By one who is a first offender":
thus the first training rule is concluded.
